outputs.L2: The endoscope system includes: an image acquisition unit configured to obtain a color image containing at least three color components; a positioning unit configured to arrange points, each associated with a pixel making up the color image, within a plane according to the color components of those points, the plane including a first axis representing a first component among the at least three color components and a second axis representing a second component among the at least three color components, the second axis intersecting the first axis; a distance-data computation unit configured to generate data relating to distances between the points associated with the respective pixels and a third axis, the third axis being defined as an axis that extends through the intersection point of the first and second axes in the plane and is not parallel to either the first axis or the second axis; and an evaluation-value computation unit configured to determine a prescribed evaluation value for the color image based on the computed distance data.

The endoscope system acquires a color image that includes at least three color components, such as red, green, and blue components. Each pixel in the acquired color image has corresponding color component values.

The system then maps points corresponding to the pixels of the image onto a plane according to their color component values. In this plane, a first axis represents one of the color components, and a second axis represents another color component. The first and second axes intersect each other, thereby defining a reference plane for evaluating the color characteristics of the image.

In addition, the system defines a third axis that passes through the intersection point of the first and second axes. This third axis is set so that it is not parallel to either the first axis or the second axis. As a result, the third axis provides a separate reference direction within the plane.

The system calculates distance data between the mapped pixel points and the third axis. Based on this distance data, the system determines an evaluation value for the color image. This evaluation value represents a characteristic of the image derived from the distribution of pixel color values relative to the third axis, and may be used to assess or process the acquired endoscopic image.
outputs.L4:
An endoscope system is configured to acquire and analyze a color image obtained during endoscopic observation. The system receives image data representing the color image and maps the pixels of that image into a predetermined color space. In this color space, a plane is defined by two selected color-component axes, such as axes corresponding to different color signals or color-difference components. Each pixel of the color image is represented as a point on this plane according to its color-component values.

The system also defines a third reference axis that is not parallel to either of the two color-component axes forming the plane. For each mapped pixel, or for a selected group of pixels, the system determines distance information indicating how far the pixel position lies from the third reference axis. These distances reflect the distribution and tendency of colors contained in the endoscopic image, such as variations associated with mucosal tissue, blood vessels, lesions, inflammation, or other observed structures.

Based on the calculated distance data, the system generates an evaluation value for the color image. The evaluation value may be obtained by statistical processing of the distance information, for example by calculating an average, total, variance, distribution ratio, or another representative value. This evaluation value provides a quantitative indication of the color characteristics of the image and can be used to assess the image objectively rather than relying solely on visual interpretation.

By converting color information into distance data relative to a reference axis and calculating an evaluation value from that data, the endoscope system enables consistent and reproducible analysis of endoscopic images. The resulting quantitative assessment can assist an operator in observing tissue condition, comparing images, detecting color changes, or supporting diagnostic evaluation during endoscopic examination.

We use it every day without thinking: *this moment, this idea, this place, this person*. The word creates a connection between what we are saying and what is happening right now.

In many ways, “this” reminds us to focus on the present. Instead of worrying about the past or rushing into the future, we can pay attention to this day, this choice, and this opportunity. Sometimes, the most important things in life are not far away—they are right here, in this moment.

Whether used in conversation, writing, or reflection, “this” gives meaning to what is near and immediate. It is simple, but powerful.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe, in patent language, an endoscope image analysis apparatus that uses at least three color components, places each pixel as a point on a plane of two components, measures distances to a nonparallel third axis, and derives an image evaluation metric.
counterfactuals.output:
An endoscope image analysis apparatus comprising:

an image acquisition unit configured to acquire an endoscopic image including a plurality of pixels, each pixel having color information represented by at least three color components;

a color component extraction unit configured to extract, for each of the plurality of pixels, first, second, and third color component values from the at least three color components;

a coordinate conversion unit configured to assign each pixel to a point on a two-dimensional color-component plane defined by a first coordinate axis corresponding to the first color component and a second coordinate axis corresponding to the second color component;

an axis-setting unit configured to define, on the two-dimensional color-component plane, a third color-component axis corresponding to the third color component, the third color-component axis being nonparallel to at least one of the first coordinate axis and the second coordinate axis;

a distance calculation unit configured to calculate, for each pixel or for each of a plurality of selected pixels, a distance on the two-dimensional color-component plane between the point assigned to the pixel and the third color-component axis; and

an evaluation metric calculation unit configured to derive an image evaluation metric for the endoscopic image based on the calculated distances.

In one embodiment, the at least three color components comprise red, green, and blue components of the endoscopic image. The coordinate conversion unit places each pixel at a position on an R-G plane using the red component value and the green component value as orthogonal coordinates, and the axis-setting unit defines a B axis corresponding to the blue component on the R-G plane, the B axis being inclined with respect to the R axis and the G axis. The distance calculation unit determines a perpendicular distance from each pixel point to the B axis, and the evaluation metric calculation unit calculates, as the image evaluation metric, a statistical value of the distances, including at least one of an average value, a median value, a variance, a standard deviation, a maximum value, a minimum value, a histogram feature, or a weighted combination thereof.

In another embodiment, the image evaluation metric is indicative of a color distribution characteristic of the endoscopic image. The metric may be used to evaluate at least one of mucosal redness, blood concentration, inflammation, lesion likelihood, image quality, observation suitability, or a degree of separation between biological tissue regions and non-biological regions.

The apparatus may further comprise a region-of-interest setting unit configured to select a region of interest in the endoscopic image, wherein the distance calculation unit calculates the distances only for pixels included in the region of interest, and the evaluation metric calculation unit derives the image evaluation metric for the region of interest.

The apparatus may further comprise a normalization unit configured to normalize the first, second, and third color component values prior to placement of the pixels on the two-dimensional color-component plane, thereby reducing influence of illumination intensity, exposure variation, or shading in the endoscopic image.

The apparatus may further comprise an output unit configured to output the image evaluation metric to at least one of a display device, a storage device, a diagnostic support module, or an endoscope control unit. The output unit may display the image evaluation metric together with the endoscopic image, or may generate a map in which pixel values correspond to the calculated distances from the third color-component axis.

A method performed by the apparatus comprises acquiring an endoscopic image; extracting at least three color component values for pixels of the image; plotting each pixel as a point on a plane defined by two of the color components; defining, on the plane, an axis corresponding to a third color component and extending in a direction nonparallel to at least one axis of the plane; calculating distances between the plotted pixel points and the third color-component axis; and calculating an image evaluation metric from the distances.

A non-transitory computer-readable storage medium may store instructions that, when executed by a processor, cause the processor to perform the foregoing method.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4
